### macOS: in the Dock while the window is open

Since v0.3.0, MuxSU on macOS has lived only in the menu bar, out of the Dock and
Command-Tab. That is right while the window is closed; but an open window that went behind
another one could only be found again through the menu bar.

The Dock icon now follows the main window:

- **It appears when the window opens**: at launch, from Open MuxSU in the menu bar, or with
  the global shortcut. Command-Tab reaches it too.
- **It goes when the window closes**: MuxSU carries on in the menu bar and switching is
  unaffected.
- The host switcher does not bring it up.

While the window is open, MuxSU also has its own menu bar, so **Command-Q quits MuxSU**, as it
does any other app. Open it again from Applications to bring switching and pairing back.

### Displays the Mac reads no serial number from can be switched on the Mac

Switching the MSI MPG 274U in 1080p from the Mac failed with "the shared display was not
found", even with the display on the Mac's screen.

Windows and macOS read different serial number fields in a display's EDID: Windows reads
this display's serial and the Mac reads none. A merge made on the PC carries the PC's serial,
and a switch required an exact match, which the Mac could never make.

Now, when no display matches exactly, one that differs only by a serial one side could not
read also counts — but only if exactly one display fits. With more than one, nothing is
switched, and two different serials never count as one display.

### The main window updates straight away after switching from the host switcher

A switch made from the host switcher used to leave the main window showing the old host until
its next scan or a manual refresh. Every window is now told as soon as a switch succeeds.

### Why the version jumps to 0.5.0

Under rule 3 in `docs/versioning.md`: where the app appears on macOS has changed (it is in the
Dock and Command-Tab while its window is open). Nothing needs setting up again, and it pairs
with v0.4.x.

### Known limitations

- When the Mac and Windows read different serial numbers from the same display (the Acer
  VG252Q reads one on both, but not the same one), the two hosts treat it as two displays.
  Asking the other host to switch that display for you may report that the shared display
  was not found.
- Unmerging does not move back the input settings and notes that were folded into the other
  identity.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed and not yet notarised with an Apple Developer ID, so
  Gatekeeper may ask you to allow it manually.
